The diagram displays the mouth opening into the pharynx, which narrows into the esophagus as a tubular structure descending through the thorax into the abdominal cavity. The stomach's walls show the three muscle layers arranged in different directions for churning and mixing food with gastric juices and hydrochloric acid. The stomach narrows at the pyloric sphincter where it transitions into the small intestine. The small intestine is depicted in three coiled sections: the duodenum receiving the common bile duct from the liver and gallbladder above, plus the pancreatic duct from the pancreas positioned behind the stomach delivering digestive enzymes and bicarbonate to neutralize stomach acid. The jejunum and ileum follow in looped coils showing their absorptive villi lining. The small intestine connects to the large intestine or colon, which ascends on the right side, crosses the abdomen horizontally, and descends on the left before terminating at the rectum and anal canal. The liver is visible above the stomach, the gallbladder tucked beneath it, and the pancreas positioned horizontally behind the stomach. The entire system is shown in anatomical position within the abdominal cavity.
